mean: down-to-earth and steady in one's work

use.how: Adverbial (脚踏实地地干) or predicate. Praises a practical, steady attitude to work or study, often set against 好高骛远 or 一步登天.

near.diff: 循序渐进 describes a method of going step by step in order; 脚踏实地 describes a person's attitude: practical, honest work, no empty ambitions.
吃苦耐劳 is about enduring hardship; 脚踏实地 is about doing real work instead of chasing what is out of reach.

cue: A new colleague talks big about changing the whole industry but never finishes a single task. What attitude should he learn instead?

ctx.s: 年轻人要{脚踏实地}，少说空话，多干实事。
ctx.en: Young people should keep their feet on the ground: less empty talk, more real work.

ctx.s: 他从普通工人做起，{脚踏实地}干了十年，终于当上了车间主任。
ctx.en: He started as an ordinary worker, put in ten years of solid work, and finally became workshop director.

ctx.s: 老师在评语里写道：该生学习{脚踏实地}，从不好高骛远。
ctx.en: The teacher wrote in the report: this student studies steadily and never aims at things beyond reach.

ctx.s: 光有远大的理想还不够，还得{脚踏实地}地去做。
ctx.en: Having big ideals isn't enough; you also have to get down and do the work.

ctx.s: “创业最需要什么？”“{脚踏实地}，别光想着融资和上市。”
ctx.en: "What does starting a business need most?" "Steady, practical work. Don't just think about raising money and going public."

ctx.s: 这家小店从没做过广告，靠着老板{脚踏实地}的经营，慢慢有了一批老顾客。
ctx.en: The little shop never advertised; through the owner's steady, honest management it gradually built up loyal customers.

bad.s: 他第一次参加比赛就拿了冠军，真是{脚踏实地}。
bad.en: (meant: he won the first contest he entered; how impressive)
bad.why: It praises slow, steady, practical effort over time, not a quick win or natural talent.

bad.s: 我们要{脚踏实地}这份工作。
bad.en: (meant: we must do this job in a practical, steady way)
bad.why: It takes no object; use it as an adverbial or predicate instead: zuò zhè fèn gōngzuò yào jiǎo tà shí dì.

mean: to keep improving what is already good
lit: already refined, yet seeking still more refinement

story.text: In the Analects, Zigong quotes a line from the Book of Songs, 'as if cut, as if filed, as if carved, as if polished', and Confucius praises him. The Song scholar Zhu Xi explained the line: a craftsman working bone or horn cuts it and then files it; one working jade or stone carves it and then polishes it. The work is already fine, yet he seeks to make it finer still. The idiom comes from Zhu Xi's words.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (精益求精的精神). Praises work, craft or service that is already good and still being refined; takes no object.

near.diff: 一丝不苟 is care over every detail of a task; 精益求精 is going on to improve something that is already good.
再接再厉 urges more effort after a success; 精益求精 is about raising the quality of a skill or a piece of work.

cue: A chef's signature dish already wins awards, yet she adjusts the recipe a little every week to make it better still. What attitude does she show?

ctx.s: 我们的产品已经不错了，但还要{精益求精}。
ctx.en: Our product is already good, but we still need to keep improving it.

ctx.s: 这位老师傅做的家具已经是全城最好的，可他还在不断{精益求精}。
ctx.en: The old master's furniture is already the best in town, yet he keeps on refining it.

ctx.s: “这版设计已经很好了，还要改？”“客户要求高，我们得{精益求精}。”
ctx.en: "This design is already very good; you're changing it again?" "The client's standards are high; we have to keep polishing."

ctx.s: 正是这种{精益求精}的工匠精神，让这个品牌闻名世界。
ctx.en: It is exactly this craftsman's drive to keep perfecting things that made the brand world-famous.

ctx.s: 她的演奏已经无可挑剔，可她还想{精益求精}，每天多练两个小时。
ctx.en: Her playing is already flawless, yet she wants to make it better still and practises two extra hours a day.

ctx.s: 酒店的服务一向口碑很好，今年又{精益求精}，推出了十几项改进。
ctx.en: The hotel's service has always been well regarded, and this year it raised the bar again with a dozen improvements.

bad.s: 这份报告错误百出，我们要{精益求精}。
bad.en: (meant: this report is full of errors; we must fix it)
bad.why: It means improving what is already good; a report full of errors simply needs correcting.

bad.s: 我想{精益求精}我的中文。
bad.en: (meant: I want to perfect my Chinese)
bad.why: It takes no object; name the field first instead, as in xué Zhōngwén yào jīng yì qiú jīng.

mean: to handle something with skill and ease
lit: what the heart conceives, the hand answers

story.text: Duke Huan of Qi was reading in his hall when Wheelwright Bian, making a wheel below, asked what he was reading. The words of the sages, said the duke. Then they are only the dregs of the ancients, said Bian. Asked to explain, he spoke of his craft: cut too slowly or too quickly and the wheel is spoiled; getting it just right is felt in the hand and answered in the heart, and he cannot put it into words or pass it even to his son. The idiom grew from this description of skill.

use.how: Predicate, often after 用起来, 做起来 or 越来越: 这把刀用起来很得心应手。 Says a tool, task or skill is handled smoothly, usually after practice; takes no object.

near.diff: 轻而易举 says a task is easy in itself; 得心应手 says the person handles it smoothly thanks to skill, practice or a well-suited tool.
熟能生巧 is the saying that practice brings skill; 得心应手 describes the smooth handling that results.

cue: After two years with the same camera, a photographer changes every setting without looking. How does the camera feel in her hands?

ctx.s: 这支笔我用了很多年，写起字来特别{得心应手}。
ctx.en: I've used this pen for years; writing with it feels completely natural.

ctx.s: 刚开始做这份工作有点紧张，现在已经{得心应手}了。
ctx.en: I was a bit nervous when I started this job, but now I handle it with ease.

ctx.s: “新软件用得惯吗？”“还不太{得心应手}，再练几天就好了。”
ctx.en: "Used to the new software yet?" "Not quite at ease with it; a few more days of practice and I will be."

ctx.s: 他在销售部干了十多年，处理客户投诉早就{得心应手}。
ctx.en: He's been in sales for over ten years; dealing with customer complaints is second nature to him.

ctx.s: 换了一把合适的球拍以后，她打起球来{得心应手}多了。
ctx.en: After switching to a racket that suits her, she plays far more comfortably.

ctx.s: 他第一次当翻译时手忙脚乱，到了第三场会议，已经能{得心应手}地应对各种提问。
ctx.en: At his first interpreting job he was flustered, but by the third meeting he was handling every question with ease.

bad.s: 这道题太简单了，谁做都{得心应手}。
bad.en: (meant: this question is so easy anyone can do it)
bad.why: The ease must come from someone's skill or practice, not from the task being simple; for a simple task say qīng ér yì jǔ.

bad.s: 他很{得心应手}电脑。
bad.en: (meant: he is good with computers)
bad.why: It takes no object; say that using the computer comes easily to him: tā yòng diànnǎo hěn dé xīn yìng shǒu.

mean: to do something perfunctorily to get it over with
lit: to go through the motions and be done with the matter

use.how: Predicate, often after 不能, 别 or 只是: 工作不能敷衍了事。 Criticises doing a task with minimal effort just to finish it; takes no object.

near.diff: 粗心大意 is carelessness by inattention; 敷衍了事 is deliberately doing the minimum to get a task off one's hands.

cue: A repairman paid to fix your heater glances at it for two minutes, tightens one screw and leaves. It breaks again that night. How did he do the job?

ctx.s: 作业要认真写，不能随便写几个字就{敷衍了事}。
ctx.en: Do your homework properly; you can't scribble a few words just to get it over with.

ctx.s: 这么重要的检查，他居然{敷衍了事}，难怪出了问题。
ctx.en: He just went through the motions on such an important inspection; no wonder things went wrong.

ctx.s: “这份总结也写得太短了吧？”“时间太紧，只好{敷衍了事}。”
ctx.en: "Isn't this summary far too short?" "Time was too tight, so I just got it done any old way."

ctx.s: 顾客投诉了三次，客服每次都{敷衍了事}，问题始终没有解决。
ctx.en: The customer complained three times; each time customer service brushed it off, and the problem was never solved.

ctx.s: 领导强调，安全检查必须一项一项做，绝不允许走过场、{敷衍了事}。
ctx.en: The manager stressed that safety checks must be done item by item; going through the motions just to finish is never allowed.

ctx.s: 那家装修公司为了赶工期{敷衍了事}，墙面没多久就开始掉皮。
ctx.en: To meet the deadline the renovation company did a slapdash job, and before long the walls began to peel.

bad.s: 他{敷衍了事}地完成了任务，受到了经理的表扬。
bad.en: (meant: he got the task done smoothly and the manager praised him)
bad.why: It is always criticism of half-hearted work, never a neutral 'got it done', so it cannot earn praise.

bad.s: 他总是{敷衍了事}他的女朋友。
bad.en: (meant: he always fobs off his girlfriend)
bad.why: The idiom takes no object and is about tasks; to fob off a person, use the plain verb fūyǎn with the person as its object.

use.how: Adverbial before a verb (大家齐心协力，把……) or predicate. Describes several people pulling together toward one goal.

near.diff: 一心一意 is one person's undivided devotion; 齐心协力 needs a group working together.
全力以赴 is putting all of one's own effort in; 齐心协力 is about many people joining their efforts.

cue: A landslide blocked the village's only road, so every family sent someone with a shovel, and by evening the road was clear. How did they manage it?

ctx.s: 只要大家{齐心协力}，这个问题一定能解决。
ctx.en: As long as we all pull together, this problem can definitely be solved.

ctx.s: 全班同学{齐心协力}，在拔河比赛中拿了第一名。
ctx.en: The whole class pulled together and won first place in the tug-of-war.

ctx.s: “这么多箱子，今天搬得完吗？”“我们几个{齐心协力}，没问题。”
ctx.en: "So many boxes; can we move them all today?" "If the few of us work together, no problem."

ctx.s: 公司上下{齐心协力}，只用三个月就完成了全年的销售任务。
ctx.en: Everyone in the company, top to bottom, worked as one and hit the whole year's sales target in just three months.

ctx.s: 这个项目能成功，离不开团队每个成员的{齐心协力}。
ctx.en: The project's success depended on every team member working together.

ctx.s: 夫妻俩{齐心协力}，把一家小面馆经营成了连锁店。
ctx.en: Working side by side, the couple turned a small noodle shop into a chain.

bad.s: 他一个人{齐心协力}地写完了整篇论文。
bad.en: (meant: he wrote the whole thesis by himself with total dedication)
bad.why: It needs several people; for one person's dedication use yī xīn yī yì or quán lì yǐ fù.

bad.s: 我们俩{齐心协力}，都喜欢看电影。
bad.en: (meant: we are of one mind; we both love films)
bad.why: It means joining efforts on a task, not sharing tastes; for shared tastes simply say your hobbies are the same.

mean: double the result with half the effort
lit: half the work, double the achievement

story.text: Mencius told his disciple Gongsun Chou that their own age was the best moment for a ruler to govern by benevolence: the people were suffering under harsh rule and would welcome relief like someone freed from hanging upside down. So, he said, a ruler who did half of what the ancients did would surely achieve twice as much; only at such a time was this so.

use.how: Predicate, often after a condition with 就能 or 会: 方法对了，学习就能事半功倍。 Says a method or condition makes effort pay off far more. Its reverse is 事倍功半.

near.diff: 一举两得 is one action bringing two separate gains; 事半功倍 is one goal reached with far less effort.
事倍功半 is the exact reverse: twice the effort for half the result. Learners often swap the two.

cue: A student stops memorising words at random, starts learning them in families by shared root, and remembers three times as many in the same hour. What has the new method done?

ctx.s: 学习方法对了，就能{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: With the right study method, you get far more out of less effort.

ctx.s: 用这个软件处理数据，可以说是{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: Processing the data with this software, you could say, doubles the output for half the work.

ctx.s: “怎么才能把单词背得快一点？”“先把词根弄清楚，会{事半功倍}。”
ctx.en: "How can I memorise words faster?" "Get the roots clear first; it will save you a lot of effort."

ctx.s: 好的工具能让工作{事半功倍}，所以这笔钱花得值。
ctx.en: Good tools make work far more efficient, so this money was well spent.

ctx.s: 先找准目标客户再去推销，往往{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: Pinning down your target customers before you start selling usually pays off far better.

ctx.s: 老师常说，与其熬夜苦读，不如睡足了再学，那样才能{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: The teacher always says it's better to sleep well and then study than to cram all night; that way the effort goes much further.

bad.s: 我花了一整天才做完这么一点，真是{事半功倍}。
bad.en: (meant: a whole day's work for so little result)
bad.why: That is the reverse, shì bèi gōng bàn; this idiom means less effort and a bigger result.

bad.s: 他是一个{事半功倍}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is an efficient person)
bad.why: It describes a method or condition paying off, not a person's character; to call someone efficient, talk about their xiàolǜ.

mean: to have a clear plan in mind beforehand
lit: to have the whole bamboo already in one's chest

story.text: The Song painter Wen Tong, also called Wen Yuke, was famous for his bamboo. His friend Su Shi wrote that to paint bamboo one must first have the complete bamboo in one's mind; then, brush in hand, gaze until the image appears and chase it at once without stopping, like a falcon swooping the instant a hare breaks cover, for if you hesitate it is gone.
story.source: 苏轼《文与可画筼筜谷偃竹记》

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (胸有成竹地说). Describes someone calm and confident because they already know how they will handle what is coming; takes no object.

near.diff: 有备无患 is a maxim that preparation prevents trouble; 胸有成竹 describes a person's confident state of mind about a plan already formed.
深思熟虑 is the process of thinking something over carefully; 胸有成竹 is the calm confidence of already knowing what to do.

cue: Before a big negotiation everyone is nervous except the lead negotiator, who smiles because she already knows every step she will take. How does she look?

ctx.s: 看他{胸有成竹}的样子，这次考试肯定准备得很好。
ctx.en: From how confident he looks, he must have prepared well for this exam.

ctx.s: 面试官问了很多难题，她都{胸有成竹}地一一回答了。
ctx.en: The interviewers asked many hard questions, and she answered each one with calm assurance.

ctx.s: “明天的演讲准备好了吗？”“放心吧，我早就{胸有成竹}了。”
ctx.en: "Are you ready for tomorrow's speech?" "Don't worry, I've had it all worked out for ages."

ctx.s: 教练对下半场早有安排，一点也不着急，显得{胸有成竹}。
ctx.en: The coach had the second half planned long ago; he wasn't worried at all and looked completely sure of himself.

ctx.s: 对装修方案他早就{胸有成竹}，连每个房间的颜色都想好了。
ctx.en: He had the renovation plan clear in his head long ago, right down to the colour of every room.

ctx.s: 大家还在争论该从哪里下手，老王已经{胸有成竹}地拿出了一份完整的计划。
ctx.en: While everyone was still arguing about where to start, Lao Wang calmly produced a complete plan.

bad.s: 我对明天的考试一点准备都没有，但还是{胸有成竹}。
bad.en: (meant: I haven't prepared at all, but I feel confident anyway)
bad.why: The confidence must rest on a plan already formed; blind confidence without preparation is a contradiction.

bad.s: 我{胸有成竹}这个计划。
bad.en: (meant: I'm sure about this plan)
bad.why: It takes no object; introduce the plan with duì: wǒ duì zhège jìhuà xiōng yǒu chéng zhú.

mean: to satisfy both sides at once
lit: both sides made whole, both made good

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often 两全其美的办法: 这是个两全其美的办法。 Describes a solution that satisfies two needs or parties that seemed to conflict; takes no object.

near.diff: 一举两得 is one action bringing two gains; 两全其美 resolves a conflict so that neither side has to lose.
十全十美 means perfect in every way; 两全其美 only means two competing needs are both met.

cue: Your parents want you home for the holidays and your boss needs you working, so you arrange to work remotely from your parents' house. What kind of solution is it?

ctx.s: 有没有{两全其美}的办法？
ctx.en: Is there a way to keep both sides happy?

ctx.s: 孩子没人照顾，工作又不能停，公司让我在家办公，真是{两全其美}。
ctx.en: No one could look after the kids and work couldn't stop, so the company let me work from home; both needs were met.

ctx.s: “我想去旅游，又不想花太多钱。”“那就去附近的小城，{两全其美}。”
ctx.en: "I want to travel, but I don't want to spend much." "Then go to a small town nearby; that covers both."

ctx.s: 公司让员工自己选上班时间，老板和员工都满意，可谓{两全其美}。
ctx.en: The company lets staff choose their own hours; bosses and staff are both satisfied, the best of both worlds.

ctx.s: 世上哪有那么多{两全其美}的事，总得放弃一样。
ctx.en: How often can you have it both ways? You always have to give something up.

ctx.s: 两家都想在自己家乡办婚礼，最后决定两地各办一场，总算{两全其美}。
ctx.en: Both families wanted the wedding in their own hometown; in the end they held one in each place, and everyone was satisfied.

bad.s: 他长得帅，学习也好，真是{两全其美}。
bad.en: (meant: he is handsome and a good student too)
bad.why: It describes a solution that meets two competing needs, not a person with two good qualities.

bad.s: 这个办法{两全其美}了我们俩。
bad.en: (meant: this plan satisfied both of us)
bad.why: It takes no object; it describes the plan itself, as in zhège bànfǎ liǎng quán qí měi.

mean: to make a good thing even better
lit: to add embroidered flowers to brocade

use.how: Predicate or object of 是, 算是: 这对他来说是锦上添花。 Says an extra makes something already good even better; often contrasted with 雪中送炭.

near.diff: 雪中送炭 is help for someone in trouble; 锦上添花 is an extra for someone or something already doing well.
画龙点睛 is the one key touch that brings the whole to life; 锦上添花 is a pleasant extra on top of what is already complete.

cue: A company already had its best year ever, and then in December it won a big new contract as well. What did the contract do for its year?

ctx.s: 这道菜本来就很好吃，撒点香菜更是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The dish was already delicious; a sprinkle of coriander makes it even better.

ctx.s: 他工作稳定，收入也不错，这次升职对他来说是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: He has a stable job and a good income; this promotion is just the icing on the cake.

ctx.s: “房子都装修好了，还要买画吗？”“挂几幅画，算是{锦上添花}吧。”
ctx.en: "The flat is all done up; do we still need to buy paintings?" "A few on the wall would be a nice extra."

ctx.s: 比赛已经赢定了，最后这个进球只是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The match was already won; that last goal was just a bonus.

ctx.s: 有钱的大公司不缺赞助，捐给它们只是{锦上添花}，不如帮帮山区的小学校。
ctx.en: Rich big companies don't lack sponsors; giving to them only adds to plenty, so better to help small schools in the mountains.

ctx.s: 婚礼已经很热闹了，朋友们又准备了一场烟花表演，真是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The wedding was already lively, and then friends put on a fireworks show, which made it even better.

bad.s: 他失业后交不起房租，朋友借给他一笔钱，真是{锦上添花}。
bad.en: (meant: a friend's loan helped him when he lost his job)
bad.why: Help for someone in trouble is xuě zhōng sòng tàn; this idiom is an extra for something already good.

bad.s: 文章已经很好了，他又加了一段废话，结果{锦上添花}，反而变差了。
bad.en: (meant: he added a needless paragraph and spoiled it)
bad.why: It means the addition made things better; an addition that spoils the result is huà shé tiān zú.

mean: to add the finishing touch that brings it to life
lit: to paint a dragon and dot in its eyes

story.text: Zhang Sengyou, a painter of the Liang dynasty, painted four dragons on the walls of Anle Temple in Jinling but left out their eyes, saying that if he painted them the dragons would fly away. People thought he was boasting and pressed him to do it. He dotted in the eyes of two: at once thunder and lightning broke the wall, and the two dragons rode the clouds up into the sky. The two without eyes are still there.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (画龙点睛之笔, 起到画龙点睛的作用). Praises one key word, line or detail that brings a whole piece of writing, speech or design to life.

near.diff: 锦上添花 is a pleasant extra on top of what is already good; 画龙点睛 is the small key touch without which the whole would stay flat.
画蛇添足 is the opposite: an addition that was not needed and spoils the whole.

cue: An essay is solid but flat, until the writer adds one striking closing sentence that makes the whole piece hit home. What did that sentence do?

ctx.s: 文章最后一句写得很好，起到了{画龙点睛}的作用。
ctx.en: The essay's last sentence is excellent; it is the finishing touch that brings the whole thing to life.

ctx.s: 这条红围巾是整套衣服的{画龙点睛}之笔。
ctx.en: This red scarf is the touch that makes the whole outfit come alive.

ctx.s: “标题还要改吗？”“要改，好标题能{画龙点睛}。”
ctx.en: "Do we still need to change the title?" "Yes. A good title can bring the whole piece to life."

ctx.s: 设计师只在白墙上挂了一幅小画，却有{画龙点睛}的效果，整个客厅一下子有了生气。
ctx.en: The designer hung just one small painting on the white wall, yet it made all the difference; the living room suddenly came alive.

ctx.s: 主持人最后那句总结{画龙点睛}，把整场讨论的意思都说透了。
ctx.en: The host's closing summary was the perfect final touch, bringing out the point of the whole discussion.

ctx.s: 这部电影的配乐很简单，却在几个关键镜头里{画龙点睛}。
ctx.en: The film's score is simple, but in a few key scenes it is exactly what brings them to life.

bad.s: 他的演讲本来就很长，最后又加了半小时，真是{画龙点睛}。
bad.en: (meant: his long speech dragged on another half hour)
bad.why: An addition that drags on or spoils is huà shé tiān zú; this idiom praises a small key touch that makes the whole better.

bad.s: 这家店的菜很好吃，结账时还送了一瓶饮料，真是{画龙点睛}。
bad.en: (meant: the free drink at the end was a nice bonus)
bad.why: A bonus on top is jǐn shàng tiān huā; this idiom needs one small key detail that brings a whole work to life.
